subject: Phase 100130: Co-Activation Associations and Hub Distillation (developer r2 staged diff)
verdict_justification: The core behavior is implemented and genuinely tested: all 531 workspace tests pass, clippy is clean, fmt is clean, and coverage passes aggregate (fn 98.54% / lines 98.42%) with all 113 reported files at or above 90% on both functions and lines. However, several claims are stronger than the code supports: the ranking-env association knobs are stored but consumed by no production path, the §7.4.5 derivative-decision log failure is silently swallowed, and expand_graph does not honor min_weight for explicit edges. These are real spec gaps rather than cosmetic ones. Remediation r1 (2026-09-19): all eight findings addressed - F-01/F-02/F-03/F-05/F-06/F-07/F-08 fixed in code+phase file; F-04 partially fixed (reinforce + hub enqueue/complete telemetry, error-propagating) with the durable resumable-queue deviation recorded as an explicit non-conformance.

findings.title: §7.4.5 anonymized-derivative decision log failure is silently swallowed
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/hub_distill.rs:361-368 calls `let _ = self.store.record_assoc_audit(...)` for the hub_distill derivative decision. A storage failure returns Ok and the admitted distilled item remains stored with no logged decision.
findings.requirement_ref: requirement.md §7.4.5 ('this determination MUST be affirmatively logged per item at the time of distillation')
findings.recommendation: Propagate the audit error (fail the distillation or surface a degraded status) so the MUST-log cannot be silently skipped; if best-effort is intentional, the requirement needs an explicit carve-out.
findings.resolution: Resolved: `HubDistillEngine::audit` now returns `Result<(), AmError>` and `distill_hub` calls it with `self.audit(...)?` (crates/clio-write/src/hub_distill.rs). A failed §7.4.5 derivative-decision log now fails the distillation instead of being discarded.

findings.title: expand_graph does not apply min_weight to explicit edges and the inline comment is wrong
findings.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_graph.rs:270-274 expands any neighbor whose observe() returns Some, commenting that observe prunes below w_min; but crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc.rs:138-139 returns Some(edge.weight) for explicit edges at any weight, so a 0.001-weight explicit edge is expanded. associations (assoc_graph.rs:60) and graph_query (assoc_graph.rs:209) do apply the min filter.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100130 Task 5 ('add neighbors with w_eff >= min_weight'); requirement.md §4.5 explicit-edge participation
findings.recommendation: Apply the policy min-weight check inside expand_ids for both kinds, or explicitly document that sticky explicit edges bypass min_weight and fix the misleading comment.
findings.resolution: Resolved: `expand_ids` now applies `if eff < self.policy.w_min { continue; }` for every edge kind (explicit included) and the misleading comment was corrected (crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_graph.rs). New test `assoc_graph_tests::t08c_expand_skips_explicit_below_min_weight` proves a 0.01-weight explicit edge is not expanded while a 0.5-weight one is.

findings.title: Coactivation pair uniqueness is application-enforced only, not by a DB constraint
findings.evidence: sql/001_core.sql:423 UNIQUE (bank_id, source_id, target_id, assoc_kind, relationship); relationship is NULL for coactivation and NULLs compare distinct, so the constraint does not prevent duplicate coactivation rows. Uniqueness holds only because reinforce_assoc_edge always writes the deterministic coactivation_id (sqlite_assoc.rs:222).
findings.recommendation: Add a partial unique index on (bank_id, source_id, target_id) WHERE assoc_kind='coactivation', or document that the deterministic id is the sole uniqueness mechanism.
findings.resolution: Resolved: added partial unique index `assoc_edges_coactivation_pair_inx` on `(bank_id, source_id, target_id) WHERE assoc_kind='coactivation'` in sql/001_core.sql; new test `assoc_edge_tests::sqlite_coactivation_pair_unique_index_blocks_duplicates` proves a second coactivation row with a different id for the same pair is rejected. Verified on live Postgres too (pg_assoc_edge_tests suite still green after schema apply).

issues.title: Ranking-env co-activation knobs are stored but consumed by no production path
issues.why_it_matters: The phase Goal and AC-100130-08 present association knobs as operator-tunable without code changes. In fact nothing reads RankingEnv.coactivation when building the retriever, so ranking_env_set(eta=...) has no effect on reinforcement or decay.
issues.impact: Operators can change eta/half_life/w_min in config and observe no behavioral change, silently. The tests pass only because they set the policy object directly.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/hybrid.rs:83-86; crates/clio-store/src/assoc.rs:47-51; grep: from_coactivation/set_assoc_policy have no non-test callers; crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_tests.rs:188-202.
issues.proposed_fix: Construct AssocPolicy from the live RankingEnv.coactivation at retriever construction (or in the retrieve handler), and add a test that patches eta via ranking_env and observes the changed growth step on retrieve.
issues.resolution: Resolved: added `HybridRetriever::with_ranking_env` / `set_ranking_env` (crates/clio-retrieve/src/hybrid.rs) which build `AssocPolicy::from_coactivation(&env.coactivation)` and apply `env.retrieval` + `recency_tau_days`. New test `assoc::assoc_tests::t12b_ranking_env_coactivation_wires_into_retriever` sets `RankingEnv.coactivation.eta=0.5`, retrieves through the production constructor, and observes a 0.5 growth step (was 0.15).

issues.title: §7.4.5 derivative-decision log failure is silently swallowed
issues.why_it_matters: requirement.md §7.4.5 states the anonymized-derivative determination MUST be affirmatively logged per item at distillation time. The code discards the log result.
issues.impact: A distilled item can be admitted and retained with no durable record of the derivative decision, so the compliance MUST is not guaranteed.
issues.proposed_fix: Propagate record_assoc_audit's error from distill_hub so the distillation fails (or reports degraded) when the decision cannot be logged.
issues.resolution: Resolved: `HubDistillEngine::audit` now returns `Result<(), AmError>` and `distill_hub` calls it with `self.audit(...)?` (crates/clio-write/src/hub_distill.rs). A failed §7.4.5 derivative-decision log now fails the distillation instead of being discarded.

issues.title: expand_graph ignores min_weight for explicit edges and the comment is inaccurate
issues.why_it_matters: Phase Task 5 requires expansion to add neighbors with w_eff >= min_weight. Explicit edges are added at any weight, unlike associations/graph_query, so weak explicit links can pull unrelated items into results.
issues.impact: Inconsistent filtering between tools; a 0.0-1.0 weight explicit edge below w_min is still expanded, defeating the min_weight bound.
issues.proposed_fix: Apply `eff < min` in expand_ids for both kinds, or explicitly document and test that sticky explicit edges intentionally bypass min_weight; fix the misleading comment.
issues.resolution: Resolved: `expand_ids` now applies `if eff < self.policy.w_min { continue; }` for every edge kind (explicit included) and the misleading comment was corrected (crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_graph.rs). New test `assoc_graph_tests::t08c_expand_skips_explicit_below_min_weight` proves a 0.01-weight explicit edge is not expanded while a 0.5-weight one is.

issues.title: hub_distill is not enqueued and reinforce/hub telemetry is incomplete
issues.why_it_matters: Task 6 says enqueue a hub_distill job drained by consolidate, and In-Scope lists reinforce/prune/hub-enqueue telemetry. Eligibility is recomputed on every consolidate with no durable queue or pending state, and reinforce emits no telemetry.
issues.impact: No queue depth/pending visibility; a crash mid-consolidate leaves no record of intended work. FR-15-spirit telemetry for reinforce is absent.
issues.proposed_fix: Implement a durable/queued hub_distill job with maintenance_status reporting and a PII-safe reinforce telemetry event, or document the deviation as a known non-conformance in the phase.
issues.resolution: Resolved with a documented non-conformance: added `assoc_reinforce` telemetry (crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc.rs) and `hub_distill_enqueue` / `hub_distill_complete` telemetry (crates/clio-write/src/hub_distill.rs), all PII-safe and error-propagating. A durable resumable hub_distill queue and `maintenance_status` pending-hub reporting were NOT implemented; the phase marks that reporting optional ('MAY') and a durable queue needs a new store table plus dual-backend/async surface beyond this slice, so the deviation is recorded explicitly in the phase Known Limitations rather than faked.

issues.title: T100130-05 durable-handoff failure test only exercises store-side validation
issues.why_it_matters: FR-17's hard requirement is fail-closed on durable handoff failure, not merely on a validation error. The test does not exercise a real handoff/DB failure.
issues.impact: A partial-reinforcement or torn-write bug would not be caught by the current suite.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a store double that fails on the second reinforce and assert retrieve returns Err with no partial-success outcome.
issues.resolution: Resolved: added `crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_durable_tests.rs` with a delegating `FaultyStore` double that fails the second `reinforce_assoc_edge` call. `t05b_mid_reinforce_failure_fails_retrieve_closed` asserts `retrieve` returns `Err` (Internal) and stops at the failing pair; `t04c_successful_retrieve_emits_reinforce_telemetry` asserts one audit per wave.

issues.title: Coactivation pair uniqueness is application-enforced only
issues.why_it_matters: Task 1 specifies one undirected coactivation weight per pair. The DB UNIQUE includes relationship, which is NULL for coactivation, so it does not enforce this.
issues.impact: Any future code path that writes a coactivation row with a non-deterministic id could create duplicates; the guarantee rests on a single helper.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a partial unique index on (bank_id, source_id, target_id) WHERE assoc_kind='coactivation', or document reliance on the deterministic id.
issues.resolution: Resolved: added partial unique index `assoc_edges_coactivation_pair_inx` on `(bank_id, source_id, target_id) WHERE assoc_kind='coactivation'` in sql/001_core.sql; new test `assoc_edge_tests::sqlite_coactivation_pair_unique_index_blocks_duplicates` proves a second coactivation row with a different id for the same pair is rejected. Verified on live Postgres too (pg_assoc_edge_tests suite still green after schema apply).

strengths: Clean separation of the pure weight-policy math (clio-store::assoc) from storage and from traversal, with the EMA engine explicitly excluded.
Atomic single-statement saturating upsert on both backends, plus a real 4-thread concurrency test proving no lost increments and no duplicate rows.
Hub distillation genuinely routes through clio_admission::gated_create and writes only on pass; reject path retains edges and creates no item.
Dual-backend parity is tested against a live Postgres, not mocked.
Honest Known Limitations section in the phase file, including the weak T100130-05 failure mode and the missing maintenance_status hub reporting.
regrets: AC-100130-08's operator-tunability claim was accepted at face value from the config round-trip test; a grep for the knob's consumer would have exposed the gap immediately.
I initially treated expand_ids' 'observe prunes below w_min' comment as true before reading observe's explicit-edge branch.
process_changes: For every config knob added, grep for a production consumer, not just a serialization test.
For every 'MUST log/emit' requirement, check that the error path is propagated rather than discarded.

Propagate the §7.4.5 derivative-log error in distill_hub (F-02).
Apply min_weight in expand_ids and fix the comment (F-03).
plan_unlimited: Implement a durable hub_distill job/queue with maintenance_status visibility and reinforce telemetry, or formally narrow the phase spec (F-04).
Add a failing-store-double durability test for FR-17 and a partial-failure test for cross-ref writes (F-05).
Add a partial unique index for coactivation pairs and a header/ownership CI check (F-06, F-08).
